transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, um… I guess it’s work. I’m a barber, and I’ve gotten to this point where I’ll do almost anything to avoid using the straight razor. Like, I’ll switch clients with someone, or say I can’t find the blade, or I’ll shove it in the drawer and pretend it’s not there. It sounds stupid saying it out loud.

And if I can’t get out of it—if I actually have to do a shave—I’m shaking the whole time. My hands, everything. It’s just… it’s gotten really hard to keep doing my job normally.
Do you feel anxious or nervous in situations outside of your job as a barber?

I mean… not that I’ve really noticed? Outside work I’m mostly okay, I think. Like, I get normal stress, traffic or bills or whatever, but that’s different. My landlord was texting me last week about the sink and I got all worked up because I hate dealing with repairs—sorry, that’s probably not what you mean.

I guess I’m not sure. It’s really the barber stuff that stands out.
Is there anything else in your life, besides using the straight razor at work, that you've been trying to avoid?

I don’t know… not really? I mean, I avoid calling my bank sometimes, but I think everyone does that, right? Last month I had to sit on hold for like forty minutes and the music was driving me crazy, and then they transferred me anyway.

But like, in the way you mean—something I’m really trying to stay away from—I can’t think of anything besides the razor stuff. That’s the one that’s messing with me.
Is your anxiety or nervousness specifically about the straight razor itself, or is it more about the act of shaving with it?

It’s… kind of both, I guess, but the open razor is what really sets it off. Like, I know it’s just a tool—I trained with it, I use clippers and scissors all day and I’m fine—but when that straight razor is sitting there open at my station, my brain just goes straight to, like, I’m going to cut myself badly or hurt the person in the chair.

And it’s stupid because I’ve used them before, you know? In school they made us practice all these angles and stretching the skin and all that, and my instructor used to say the blade doesn’t do anything you don’t make it do. But when I’m there with a real client, it doesn’t feel that way. It feels dangerous just being in my hand.
When you think about the straight razor, are you more worried about accidentally cutting yourself or the person you're shaving?

Honestly, it’s both, but maybe more the person in the chair? I mean, cutting myself would be bad too, obviously—like if the blade slipped on my thumb or something—but when I picture it, it’s usually that I’m going to hurt somebody’s face badly.

And I know that sounds dramatic. It’s just a tool, I trained with it, I use clippers all day and I’m fine. But when that straight razor is open on my station, it feels like… like something terrible is about to happen, like I’m going to cut them or cut myself before I can stop it.
Is your anxiety about using the straight razor less when you're just handling it by yourself, versus when you're actually shaving a client?

Yeah… I mean, a little, I guess. If I’m just moving it or cleaning up, it’s not as bad, but the second it’s open at my station, even before I’m actually shaving someone, I get that feeling.

It’s weird because I know it’s just a tool, and I trained with it. I can use clippers all day, scissors, no problem. Like, I’ve even nicked myself with scissors before and didn’t freak out. But with the straight razor sitting there open, my head goes straight to, I’m about to hurt somebody, or I’m going to cut myself badly. It just feels… way more dangerous than it probably is.
Does your anxiety about the straight razor increase when you think about being responsible for someone else's safety while shaving them?

Yeah, it does. When it’s just me, I can kind of tell myself, like, okay, it’s just sitting there, it’s a tool, I was trained on it. But once I think about someone’s face being right there and me being the one responsible, it ramps up fast.

I use clippers all day and scissors and I’m fine, and honestly I can talk to clients about their whole life while I’m doing a fade, no problem. People tell you everything in the chair, you know? But if that straight razor is open at my station, my mind goes straight to, like, I’m about to hurt this person or I’m going to cut myself badly. It feels way more dangerous than it should.
Does your anxiety about the straight razor start when you're preparing to shave someone, or is it already present when you're just thinking about using it later in the day?

It can start before I’m actually doing it, yeah. Like the second I hear a client ask for a razor shave, my chest kind of tightens up and my hands get sweaty, before I’ve even picked anything up.

And then if I see the blade flipped open, that’s when it really hits—like my body just wants to step back from it. It’s not even like I’ve had time to think it through. It’s just there. I’ll be standing at my station thinking about the rest of the haircut, or sometimes a client’s talking about sports or their weekend or whatever, and then they mention the razor and my whole focus just goes there.
Have you ever had a bad experience with a straight razor in the past that might be contributing to your anxiety about using it now?

I mean… not that I can really point to. Like, I didn’t have some big accident with one or anything that I remember.

I did training with them, obviously, and everybody kind of treats the straight razor like this serious thing, you know? Like in school they’d always stress being careful, steady hand, don’t rush, all that. And I remember watching older barbers do it like it was nothing, which honestly made me feel kind of stupid for getting so worked up.

But, no… I don’t think there was one bad experience where I got cut badly or hurt somebody. At least not that I can think of.
Is your anxiety about the straight razor more about the fear of it as an object, or about the responsibility of using it correctly on someone else?

It’s kind of both, I guess, but the open razor itself really sets it off. Like, I know in my head it’s just a tool, and I was trained with it. I mean, I use clippers all day, scissors too, and I don’t sit there thinking every second that I’m going to mess someone up.

But when that straight razor is sitting open at my station, it’s like my brain jumps straight to, “I’m about to hurt this person,” or “I’m going to cut myself badly.” And then, you know, the responsibility part makes it worse because it’s somebody’s face, and people trust you in the chair. People are relaxed, talking about their kids or their job or whatever, and I’m standing there trying not to think about this blade being right there. So… yeah, the object freaks me out, but using it on someone makes it feel way more intense.
Does your anxiety about the straight razor happen when you're just thinking about using it on a client, even before you've started the shave?

Yeah, it does. Like before I’ve even started, if I just know a client wants the razor shave, it kind of kicks in right away.

I’ll hear them say it and my chest tightens, my hands get sweaty, and I’m already thinking about the razor sitting there. Sometimes it’s literally just seeing the blade flipped open that does it, like my body wants to lean back or get away before I’ve even had time to think about it.

It’s weird because I can be having a normal conversation with them, like they’re talking about their weekend or whatever, and then the second the razor comes into it, that’s all I can focus on.
Do you think about what could happen if you were to make a mistake while shaving someone with the straight razor?

Yeah… I do. I mean, that’s kind of where my mind goes right away.

Like, I know it’s just a tool, and I trained with it. I can use clippers all day, scissors, all that, and I’m not thinking every second that something terrible is going to happen. But with the straight razor, especially when it’s just sitting there open at my station, my brain goes straight to, like, what if I slip? What if I hurt this guy? What if I cut myself badly?

And it’s stupid because some barbers make it look so easy, like it’s just part of the routine. I used to watch this older guy at one shop do shaves while talking about baseball the whole time, not even looking stressed, and I’d be standing there thinking, how are you that calm with that blade right there?

So yeah… I definitely think about what could happen if I made a mistake. That’s pretty much the main thing I can’t get out of my head.
Do you feel anxious around other sharp objects, like knives or scissors, when you're not at work?

Not really in the same way. Like, I use scissors and clippers all day, and I don’t usually get stuck on them like that. Even kitchen knives or whatever… I mean, I’m careful, but it’s not that same feeling.

It’s really the straight razor when it’s open, especially at my station. I know it’s just a tool, I trained with it, and other barbers use it like it’s nothing. But when it’s sitting there open, my head just goes straight to, like, I’m about to hurt somebody, or I’m going to cut myself badly.

Which is weird, because scissors are sharp too, obviously. I had this one pair I spent way too much money on, and I was more worried about dropping them and ruining the edge than hurting someone. But with the razor, it’s different. It feels more… immediate, I guess. Like the danger is right there.
Is your anxiety about the straight razor mostly because you're afraid of hurting the person you're shaving?

Yeah, mostly that… hurting the person in the chair. Like, I know it’s a tool, I trained with it, and I can use clippers all day without getting like this.

But when that straight razor is sitting open at my station, it’s like my brain just jumps to, I’m about to hurt this guy, or I’m going to cut myself badly. And then I start thinking about how close you are to their face and neck, and—sorry, I know that’s obvious, it’s literally the job—but it just feels different than other tools. It feels like one tiny mistake could be really bad.
Do you feel anxious when handling other sharp objects at work, like scissors or clippers, in the same way you do with the straight razor?

No, not really the same way. I mean, scissors are sharp, clippers can nick someone, sure, and I use them all day without thinking about it too much.

It’s specifically when the straight razor is open at my station. Like, I know it’s just a tool, I trained with it, I’m supposed to know what I’m doing… but my brain just flips into this thing where it feels like I’m about to hurt somebody, or I’m going to cut myself badly.

Which is annoying, because other guys in the shop just pick it up like it’s nothing, and I’ll be standing there thinking about the angle of the blade and the client moving suddenly, and then I’m not even thinking about the haircut anymore. So yeah, scissors and clippers don’t hit me like that. It’s the razor.
Have you ever had a traumatic experience related to a straight razor or shaving in the past?

I don’t think so… not like, some big incident where someone got cut badly or anything. At least nothing I can point to and say, “that’s when it started.”

I mean, shaving was always kind of treated like this serious thing in school, you know? Like they’d tell you to respect the blade, don’t rush, keep your hand steady, all that. And one of my instructors had this whole dramatic way of talking about razors—he was a good teacher, but he’d make everything sound like life or death. Actually, he used to do that with sanitation rules too, like if your station wasn’t spotless he’d act like the health department was hiding in the ceiling tiles.

But no, I don’t remember a traumatic thing with a straight razor. It’s more like… I know what could happen, and my head gets stuck on that.
Do you think your anxiety about the straight razor would decrease if you were only using it on yourself?

Maybe a little? I mean, if it’s just me, there isn’t that same thing of someone sitting there trusting me, you know, like with their neck right there. But I don’t think it would go away.

It’s still that straight razor being open. I know it’s just a tool, I trained with it, and I can use clippers all day without getting worked up, but when that razor is sitting there at my station my mind goes straight to, like, I’m going to hurt somebody or I’m going to cut myself badly.

Actually I’ve tried thinking, “Well, just practice at home,” and then I end up watching videos or checking the blade angle over and over—sorry, that’s not really what you asked. But yeah, using it on myself might take the client part out of it, but the razor itself still freaks me out.
Would you feel anxious about using a straight razor if you were not a barber?

Yeah… I think I still would. I mean, maybe it wouldn’t come up as much if I wasn’t doing barbering every day, obviously, because it wouldn’t be sitting right there at my station next to the combs and towels and all that.

But the thing is, I know it’s just a tool, and I trained with it, and I can use clippers all day without getting like this. It’s just when the straight razor is open—like, just open and there—it feels like I’m suddenly about to hurt somebody or cut myself badly.

So even if I had some totally different job, I think if someone handed me one, I’d still get that same feeling. Maybe I’d have more excuse to avoid it, I guess.
Would your anxiety about the straight razor be the same if you were using it in a non-professional setting?

Probably not exactly the same, but pretty close. Like, if it was just at home or something, maybe there’s less pressure because nobody’s paying me and it’s not my chair, my station, all that.

But the thing is, it’s the razor itself that gets me. I know it’s just a tool, I trained with it, and I can use clippers all day without even thinking twice. But when that straight razor is open—just sitting there—it feels like I’m about to hurt somebody or cut myself badly.

It’s weird, because I can clean up a fade and be totally fine, and then that one tool changes the whole feeling. So yeah, non-professional setting might lower the “barber” pressure, but I don’t think it would make me comfortable with it.
Would your anxiety about the straight razor decrease significantly if you were no longer working as a barber?

I mean… yeah, it might decrease some if I wasn’t around it every day. Like if I didn’t have it sitting there at my station, right next to everything else, I probably wouldn’t be set off as often.

But I don’t think it would disappear. It’s not just the job part. I know it’s just a tool, I trained with it, and I can use clippers all day without getting like this. But when that straight razor is sitting open, my brain just goes to, like, I’m about to hurt somebody or cut myself badly.

So quitting barbering would maybe make it easier to avoid, I guess… but the razor itself would still bother me.

Which is weird, because scissors are sharp too, obviously. I had this one pair I spent way too much money on, and I was more worried about dropping them and ruining the edge than hurting someone. But with the razor, it’s different. It feels more… immediate, I guess. Like the danger is right there.
